chunks: "I'll draw it left to right as a loop. On the far left, a reference clock, f ref, coming from a crystal. It goes into a phase-frequency detector, the PFD.
The PFD has a second input that comes from the feedback path.
Its outputs, UP and DOWN pulses, go into a charge pump, which outputs current into a loop filter, then a resistor and capacitor to ground.
The loop filter's output, the control voltage, goes into the VCO. The VCO's output is the PLL output, f out.
Then I take a branch off that output and send it back through a divide-by-N block, and the divided clock goes into the second input of the phase detector. That closes the loop.
I'd label the signals as I go: f ref, UP and DOWN, current from the charge pump, V control, f out, and f out over N.
And next to it I write the lock condition: when locked, f out over N equals f ref, so f out equals N times f ref.

If they want a simpler version, I can collapse the PFD, charge pump and filter into 'phase detector' and 'low-pass filter', so it's just three blocks around the loop: phase detector, loop filter, VCO, plus the divider.
And I can redraw it as a control block diagram, with the phase detector gain, the filter, the VCO as an integrator, K vco over s, and the divide-by-N in the feedback path."
